players.product: NovaLT and Frame 5 gas turbines plus Brush generators for behind-the-meter data-center power (Chart Industries thermal management added July 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: Baker Hughes' 10-K: the transaction price allocated to unsatisfied (or partially unsatisfied) remaining performance obligations was $35.9 billion as of December 31, 2025; the company expects to recognize approximately 59%, 74% and 89% of it as revenue within 2, 5 and 15 years, respectively.
quarterly_data.figure: RPO $35.9 billion as of December 31, 2025 (~59% within 2 years, 74% within 5 years, 89% within 15 years)

quarterly_data.signal: Baker Hughes' 10-K names GE Vernova and GE Aerospace as direct suppliers under long-term contractual frameworks: a heavy duty gas turbine distribution and supply agreement that licenses certain GE Vernova intellectual property to Baker Hughes (referred to as its long-term supply agreement for heavy-duty gas turbines), and a second amended and restated supply and technology development agreement with GE Vernova, GE Aerospace and the aeroderivative joint venture (Aero JV) governing the supply of certain aeroderivative technology. The Aero JV is jointly controlled by GE Vernova and Baker Hughes (50% each); Baker Hughes' purchases from the Aero JV (JV purchases, not purchases from GE Vernova directly) were $800 million, $698 million and $517 million in 2025, 2024 and 2023.
quarterly_data.figure: purchases from the Aero JV $800 million (2025), $698 million (2024), $517 million (2023)

quarterly_data.signal: Baker Hughes' 10-K capital expenditures by segment: IET $325 million in 2025 versus $284 million in 2024 and $229 million in 2023; total $1,273 million in 2025 (OFSE $887 million). The 10-K estimates 2026 capital expenditures at up to 5% of annual revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: IET capex $325 million (2025) vs $284 million (2024); total capex $1,273 million (2025)
